items.title: Section: Mutual Agreement Opens — Striking a Genuine Bargain: Material Support in Exchange for Honouring Parents and the Three Jewels

items.zh: 云何菩薩共立要契方便善巧？謂諸菩薩，若見有情求飲食等十資身具，即便共彼立要契言：汝等若能知父母恩，恭敬供養，及諸沙門婆羅門等，廣說如前，乃至若能受持淨戒；如是我當隨汝所欲，施飲食等諸資身具，如其不能，我不施汝。如是菩薩，若見有情來求種種田事、宅事、諸闤闠事、王事、域事、財事、穀事，或有來求諸工業處及諸明處，或有來求共為朋友，或有來求共結婚媾，或有來求共作邑會，或有來求助營事業，菩薩共彼立要契言：汝等若能知父母恩，恭敬供養，如前廣說：如是我當施汝田宅，廣說乃至助營事業。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's skilful means of mutual agreement? Bodhisattvas who, seeing a being request any of the ten basic necessities such as food and drink, immediately strike this agreement with them: "If you are able to recognise your debt to your parents and honour them with reverence, and likewise honour renunciants and brahmins" — stated in full as before — "up to being able to uphold pure precepts, then I will provide you with food, drink, and the other necessities according to your wish; if you are unable to do this, I will not provide them to you." Likewise, bodhisattvas who see a being come requesting land, housing, marketplace dealings, government affairs, community matters, wealth, or grain, or requesting instruction in some skilled trade or one of the branches of classical learning, or requesting friendship, marriage, a communal gathering, or help running a business, strike this same agreement with them: "If you are able to recognise your debt to your parents and honour them with reverence" — stated in full as before — "then I will provide you with land and housing," and so on up through help running a business.

items.title: Section: Mutual Agreement Closes — Rescue From Legal Danger, Fear, Frustrated Desire, and Illness, All Conditioned on the Very Same Bargain

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若見有情有諸愆犯，或被舉訟；或作種種不饒益事，為他所拘，將欲刑縛、斷截、撾打、毀辱、迫脅、驅擯、流移；或他所執，欲捶、縛、賣。菩薩爾時隨能隨力立要契言：汝等若能知父母恩，恭敬供養，如前廣說；如是我當方便救汝，令脫斯難。又諸菩薩，若見有情遭遇種種王賊、水火、人及非人、不活、惡名諸怖畏等，爾時菩薩立要契言：汝等若能知父母恩，恭敬供養，如前廣說；如是我當方便救汝，令免斯畏。又諸菩薩，若見有情欲所愛會，求非愛離，爾時菩薩立要契言：汝等若能知父母恩，恭敬供養，如前廣說；如是我當遂汝所願，令所愛會及非愛離。又諸菩薩，若見有情為疾所苦，立要契言：汝等若能知父母恩，恭敬供養，如前廣說；如是我當救汝病苦，令得安樂。彼諸有情，既為菩薩如是立要，於諸善品速疾受學，於諸惡品速疾除斷，菩薩皆能遂其所願。當知是名菩薩共立要契方便善巧。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas who see a being facing accusation, arrest, punishment, mutilation, beating, humiliation, coercion, exile, or captivity for some wrongdoing strike this agreement with them, according to their own strength and ability: "If you are able to recognise your debt to your parents and honour them" — stated in full as before — "then I will find a way to rescue you from this danger." Bodhisattvas who see a being facing terror from kings, bandits, flood, fire, human or nonhuman threat, starvation, or damaged reputation strike this same agreement: "...then I will find a way to rescue you from this fear." Bodhisattvas who see a being desperate to be united with what they love or separated from what they loathe strike this same agreement: "...then I will fulfil your wish, uniting you with what you love and separating you from what you loathe." Bodhisattvas who see a being suffering from illness strike this agreement: "...then I will rescue you from this suffering and bring you ease." Once such beings, having struck this agreement with the bodhisattva, swiftly take up wholesome conduct and swiftly abandon unwholesome conduct, bodhisattvas fulfil every one of their wishes in turn. One should understand this to be called a bodhisattva's skilful means of mutual agreement.

items.title: Section: Skilful Withholding Opens — a Bodhisattva's Deliberate, Temporary Refusal, Compassion Never Actually Wavering Underneath It

items.zh: 云何菩薩異分意樂方便善巧？謂諸菩薩與諸有情立要契已，彼諸有情於上所說彼彼事中，不如所欲速疾修行，菩薩爾時於如上說彼所求事，皆不施與。唯為利益彼有情故，非餘意樂而不施彼。如是於其諸厄難處、諸怖畏處、欲所愛會、求非愛離、病苦所惱諸有情類，權時棄捨。唯為利益彼有情故，非異意樂而棄捨之、非異意樂而不救拔。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's skilful means of differing aspiration? Bodhisattvas who, having struck an agreement with beings, find that those beings do not swiftly practice as promised in each of the matters already described, at that time withhold every one of the things those beings had requested. This is done purely for the benefit of those beings, never from any other motivation withholding it from them. In just this way, towards beings facing danger, fear, frustrated desire, or the affliction of illness, bodhisattvas temporarily set the matter aside. This is done purely for the benefit of those beings — never from a genuinely different motivation that abandons them, and never from a genuinely different motivation that fails to rescue them.

items.zh: 如是菩薩，於諸有情方便現行剛捍業時，唯為利益，非餘意樂。漸令餘時如其所欲，斷除諸惡，修學諸善，是故方便權時棄捨。

items.title: Section: Skilful Withholding Extended to Close Friends Through Feigned Anger — and the Startling License to Depose a Corrupt Official or Forcibly Reclaim Stolen Monastery Property

items.zh: 若諸有情於菩薩所，雖無所求，亦無眾難，廣說乃至無諸病苦，而與菩薩先為親厚。菩薩於彼隨宜勸導，斷諸惡法，修諸善法。所謂令彼知父母恩，恭敬供養，廣說乃至於淨尸羅隨順受學。若彼有情雖蒙菩薩如是勸導，故肆輕躁而不奉行，菩薩爾時自現憤責，唯欲利益，非憤意樂。於諸所作悉現乖背，唯為利益，非背意樂。或於一類，現與世間不饒益事，唯為利益，非損意樂。如是菩薩，於諸有情現外所作，與內意樂相不同分；由是因緣，方便安處，令彼有情漸斷諸惡、漸修諸善。是故菩薩如是調伏有情方便，名為菩薩異分意樂方便善巧。
items.en: Should beings who have no request and face no crisis whatsoever towards a bodhisattva, yet who share a genuine closeness with that bodhisattva, receive from the bodhisattva guidance suited to the occasion, encouraging the abandonment of unwholesome conduct and the cultivation of wholesome conduct — should such beings, despite receiving this guidance, willfully and carelessly disregard it and fail to follow through, the bodhisattva then displays genuine anger and reproach, wishing only to benefit them, never from an actual angry motivation. They oppose whatever such beings undertake, wishing only to benefit them, never from an actual motivation of opposition. Or, towards a certain kind of being, they inflict something that appears, in worldly terms, genuinely harmful, wishing only to benefit them, never from an actual motivation to harm. In this way, bodhisattvas display outward conduct towards beings that genuinely differs from their own inward motivation; through this very cause and condition, skilfully settling such beings, they cause them to gradually abandon what is unwholesome and gradually cultivate what is wholesome. This method by which bodhisattvas tame beings is therefore called a bodhisattva's skilful means of differing aspiration.

blocks.text: Two of the outward skilful means that may surprise you. The bodhisattva makes bargains, and sometimes withholds help on purpose. Read them with the motive in view: compassion that never wavers underneath.

Venerable Miào Jìng: 要 (yào) means seeking. Beings seek something, the bodhisattva seeks something, and both agree: it is a contract. "If you can recognise your debt to your parents and honour them, and renunciants and brahmins, … up to upholding pure precepts", then help follows. Master Cháng Bǎi: a "village gathering" means something like a lay Buddhist society inviting a teacher.

subs.head: Help that comes with a condition

blocks.text: "Having made this agreement, they swiftly train in wholesome qualities and swiftly cut off unwholesome ones." Master Cháng Bǎi gives the example: "then I will help you get out of the lawsuit, so you need not go to prison."
Venerable Miào Jìng: the contract is signed; they promised to honour their parents but don't, so the bodhisattva temporarily does not help. It is a deliberate pause, not anger.

When bodhisattvas act harshly towards beings in this way, it is solely for their benefit, with no other motive; gradually, at another time, beings come to give up evil and train in good as they wish. So the bodhisattva sets them aside only for the moment.

"Bodhisattvas display outward conduct towards beings that differs from their inner intention, thereby settling beings." This extends even to removing a corrupt official's power. Master Cháng Bǎi: this stops one side's evil and the other's suffering, yet such an act only resembles a violation; it is done from compassion.

Like the "skilful exceptions" of Days 361–362, this passage is about the bodhisattva's motive and wisdom, not a licence for anyone to coerce others. The treatise insists that the inner intention stays compassionate throughout.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "mutual agreement (要契)"?
options: "yào" means seeking — beings seek something, the bodhisattva seeks something, both agree: a contract between them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "yào" means seeking — beings seek something, the bodhisattva seeks something, and both agree; it is a contract the bodhisattva and beings make together.

quiz.q: What condition does the bodhisattva set for beings seeking necessities?
options: if they recognise their debt to parents, honour them and renunciants, up to upholding pure precepts, then the bodhisattva will give
quiz.why: "If you can recognise your debt to your parents and honour them, and renunciants and brahmins, … up to upholding pure precepts, I will provide what you wish; if not, I will not." Venerable Miào Jìng: beings ask for the ten necessities; the bodhisattva asks that they recognise their parents' kindness and honour them.

quiz.q: After beings make such an agreement with the bodhisattva, what results?
options: they swiftly take up good and cut off evil, and the bodhisattva fulfils their wishes
quiz.why: "Having made this agreement, they swiftly train in wholesome qualities and swiftly cut off unwholesome ones, and the bodhisattva fulfils their wishes." Venerable Miào Jìng: feeling the bodhisattva is willing to help, they quickly follow the teaching.

quiz.q: What does "skilful means of differing aspiration" mean?
options: outward conduct differs from inner intention — withholding, anger, opposition outside, only benefit inside
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas display outward conduct towards beings that differs from their inner intention, thereby settling beings so they gradually abandon evil and cultivate good." Venerable Miào Jìng: inner intention and outward action differ — and this too is skilful means.

quiz.q: When beings don't keep the agreement and the bodhisattva withholds, how does Venerable Miào Jìng describe it?
options: the contract is signed, they promised to honour parents but don't; the bodhisattva temporarily withholds — seemingly unkind, inwardly still benefiting them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the contract is signed — they promised to honour their parents but don't; the bodhisattva temporarily doesn't grant their wish, seeming unkind outwardly while inwardly still benefiting them.

quiz.q: "Towards a certain kind of being, inflicting something harmful in worldly terms" — such as deposing a corrupt official. How do the lectures assess it?
options: Cháng Bǎi: taking their power frees both sides, yet it resembles the karmic path of anger; Miào Jìng: precept-holding bodhisattvas may engage in politics, but beginners probably can't — it takes great merit and wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: removing their power stops one side's evil and the other's suffering — yet such an act resembles a violation along the karmic path of anger. Venerable Miào Jìng: bodhisattvas with the precepts may take part in politics, but beginners probably can't — it requires great merit and wisdom.
